scope.subject: Forward-looking native recorder contract for validation discovery, execution outcomes, and durable recovery evidence.

historical_inputs.finding: The ordered discovery vector, exactly-once outcome mapping, declared labels, and summary reconciliation were not retained.
A count and digest cannot replace an unavailable ordered discovery vector; 1,049 canonical headers did not identify the one extra outcome reported by a 1,050-test summary.
The sole historical execution is adverse evidence only and is bound to b789b68e7d6a741e0b85a3ac33cbce846e1e32c9 / b909b7b7e374bff22912059387ef0fe639498af6.
The rejected 41950b74bdec2b6e1c48ee7f5ef3ce947d0c8378 fixture candidate remains immutable adverse evidence.

problem_binding.non_retroactivity: This contract never reconstructs, normalizes, re-labels, or upgrades historical evidence. Receipts captured before this contract are legacy evidence and remain unqualified for its invariants unless a contemporaneous, separately verified native receipt exists.

portable_workflow_reuse: Use repository-relative portable paths and reject absolute, traversal, symlink, junction, and reserved-name paths, consistent with src/hive_mind_os/receipts.py.
Use canonical UTF-8 JSON and content digests for declared material, consistent with src/hive_mind_os/autopilot_workflow.py and src/hive_mind_os/receipts.py.
Use a repository-resident control-plane adapter behind a versioned contract; no recorder may execute untrusted target-repository code or acquire ambient authority.
Use the control plane's idempotency, lease, checkpoint, bounded-recovery, and independent-receipt concepts rather than chat history as state.
architecture_alignment.adapter_boundary: The recorder is a native validation adapter in the execution/evidence boundary. It accepts a sealed runner contract and emits evidence; it does not decide policy, judge results, promote candidates, mutate plans, or treat a validation receipt as a court verdict.

contract.canonicalization: UTF-8 JSON, sorted object keys, compact separators, no NaN; all listed sha256 digests are sha256 over those canonical bytes unless a field says otherwise.

session_identity.session_id: UUIDv7 generated before discovery; immutable and unique in the receipt store.
session_identity.idempotency_key: sha256 of the sealed runner contract, target binding, declared discovery selector, parser grammar digest, and label-vocabulary digest. A duplicate key may return the same committed session only after byte-for-byte binding comparison; it may never append a second execution to that session.
session_identity.attempt_id: A new recovery revalidation attempt has a new session_id and explicit predecessor_session_digest. It never silently overwrites or merges a prior attempt.

required_before_execution: repository_identity, source_commit, source_tree, declared_command, working_directory, execution_sandbox, interpreter_binding, environment_allowlist, discovery_selector, parser_grammar, terminal_label_vocabulary, timeout_and_budget, retention_policy, authority_reference

source_binding.repository_identity: canonical repository identity plus configured remote identity, when a remote exists
source_binding.source_tree: tree object ID independently resolved from source_commit before launch
source_binding.worktree_digest: digest of a sorted tracked-file manifest after checkout, excluding recorder-private output paths
source_binding.plan_or_contract_digest: the governing validation plan/contract digest; absent authority fails closed

runtime_binding.interpreter: executable path class, file digest where locally readable, implementation, exact version, ABI, and invocation arguments
runtime_binding.environment: OS, architecture, locale, timezone, container/sandbox image digest or explicit absence, network policy, resource limits, and an allowlisted map of environment variable names to privacy-safe value digests
runtime_binding.command: array arguments only, resolved working directory, approved executable identity, timeout, and runner-adapter version/digest
runtime_binding.forbidden: ambient environment capture, unpinned target checkout, mutable source after discovery, and undeclared executable substitution

record.test_id: canonical opaque runner test identifier; exact Unicode code points are preserved
record.source_location: optional portable source reference, informational only

invariants: Discovery completes and its vector is sealed before the runner receives permission to execute.
The vector is a complete ordered array, not only a count, first/last value, or digest.
test_id is nonempty and unique; duplicate IDs, invalid UTF-8, or discovery error produce a blocked session with no success claim.
discovery_vector_digest is sha256 over the complete canonical vector and discovery_count equals its length.
The runner receives the vector digest and must emit outcomes only for IDs in that vector.
ordered_discovery_vector.retention: The complete vector is a content-addressed retained artifact referenced by digest and portable path in the terminal receipt.

record.discovery_id: integer referencing one discovery vector record
record.test_id: must exactly equal the referenced discovery record
record.terminal_kind: PASS | FAIL | ERROR | SKIP_EXPLICIT | SKIP_CLASS | SKIP_LIFECYCLE | EXPECTED_FAILURE | UNEXPECTED_SUCCESS | NOT_RUN_SESSION_ABORTED | NOT_RUN_POLICY_BLOCKED
record.event_ordinal: strictly increasing integer in the parsed event stream
record.occurred_at: RFC3339 UTC timestamp supplied by the recorder
record.reason_code: required for every skip, not-run, timeout, or cancellation kind; selected from declared machine-readable codes
record.diagnostic_refs: zero or more redacted artifact references; never raw secret values

exactly_once_invariants: Every selected discovery ID has exactly one and only one terminal ledger record.
Every excluded_by_declared_selector ID has exactly one NOT_RUN_POLICY_BLOCKED record naming the sealed selector reason; it is not counted as executed.
A class-level skip is represented by one SKIP_CLASS record for every affected discovery ID, even when the underlying framework emits no method header.
A lifecycle/setup/teardown skip or cancellation is represented by one SKIP_LIFECYCLE record for every affected ID, with lifecycle phase and reason code.
If a session aborts after discovery, every selected ID without an earlier terminal event receives NOT_RUN_SESSION_ABORTED with the same immutable abort event reference; no missing ID is tolerated.
Duplicate, unknown, out-of-order, or contradictory outcomes fail receipt finalization. A terminal receipt with such a condition is invalid, not partially successful.
terminal_outcome_ledger.meaning: NOT_RUN_SESSION_ABORTED and NOT_RUN_POLICY_BLOCKED are terminal accounting states, never passing test results and never evidence that a validation command completed.

label_vocabulary.declaration: A versioned array sealed before discovery. Each entry has label_key, terminal_kind, grammar token or structured event code, reason-code requirements, and whether it is legal on a class or lifecycle boundary.
label_vocabulary.digest: label_vocabulary_digest is recorded in the runner contract, raw parser receipt, and final receipt.
invariants: One label maps to one terminal_kind in one grammar version; aliases and fallback stripping are forbidden.
Free-text warning, deprecation, or skip reason output is diagnostic data, not a terminal label unless its structured label key was declared beforehand.
A changed vocabulary changes the idempotency key and requires a new session.

capture.streams: stdout, stderr, runner-events, recorder-events, and process-exit are captured with stream ordinal, byte length, chunk hash chain, and final digest.
capture.privacy: The capture boundary computes a protected raw-stream HMAC before redaction. The normal receipt stores only that keyed digest identifier, byte counts, and sha256 digests of retained redacted streams; raw secret-bearing bytes never enter the repository receipt store.
capture.redaction: An approved versioned redaction policy runs before durable repository retention. It replaces matches with deterministic typed placeholders, preserves line/event boundaries, records redaction count and policy digest, and fails closed on scanner failure, invalid encoding, or grammar-affecting redaction. Access to any short-lived protected raw spool requires separate secret-store authority.

grammar.name: hive-mind-validation-event-jsonl-v1
grammar.digest: parser_grammar_digest binds an immutable grammar document and parser adapter digest before execution
grammar.wire_format: One UTF-8 JSON object per LF-delimited record. Each record contains schema_version, event_ordinal, event_kind, session_id, and event payload. event_kind is DISCOVERY_SEALED, OUTCOME, CLASS_SKIP, LIFECYCLE_SKIP, SESSION_ABORT, SUMMARY, or PROCESS_EXIT.
parser_rules: event_ordinal starts at zero and increments by one with no gaps or duplicates.
DISCOVERY_SEALED appears exactly once before any outcome and carries discovery_vector_digest and count.
OUTCOME, CLASS_SKIP, and LIFECYCLE_SKIP normalize only through declared label vocabulary into one ledger record per discovery ID.
SESSION_ABORT causes explicit not-run ledger records for all remaining selected IDs; it cannot terminate parsing successfully without process-exit evidence.
SUMMARY is parsed only after the ledger is complete and is reconciled rather than trusted as the source of truth.
Unparseable bytes, unknown event kinds, unknown labels, malformed JSON, duplicate terminal events, or stream/trailer digest mismatch invalidate finalization.
grammar.human_text: Verbose framework text is retained as redacted diagnostic output only. It is not an authoritative parser input in v1, eliminating ambiguous inline labels such as the historical warning and skip-reason headers.

required_equations: executed_count = count(PASS, FAIL, ERROR, SKIP_EXPLICIT, SKIP_CLASS, SKIP_LIFECYCLE, EXPECTED_FAILURE, UNEXPECTED_SUCCESS)
runner summary executed/failed/error/skipped/expected-failure totals, when supplied, equal the corresponding ledger totals
summary_reconciliation.failure_behavior: Missing or inconsistent summary is retained as an adverse parser finding. It prevents a successful validation result and cannot be repaired by post-hoc aggregation.

fields: receipt_id, session_id, idempotency_key, state, authority_reference, runner_contract_digest, source_binding, runtime_binding, discovery_artifact, ledger_artifact, parser_artifact, redacted_stream_artifacts, reconciliation, process_exit, privacy, retention, recovery_linkage, receipt_digest
root_record.result_states: VALIDATED_SUCCEEDED | VALIDATED_FAILED | BLOCKED | INVALID_CAPTURE. Only the first two mean all recorder invariants were met; VALIDATED_FAILED is an accurately captured adverse validation result.

receipt_bundle.artifact_manifest: Every artifact has portable relative path, media type, byte length, sha256, producer identity, and retention class. The final receipt includes a sorted manifest digest and no artifact is implied by prose.
atomic_commit_protocol: Create a new session-private staging directory using exclusive creation; reject preexisting session_id or receipt_id.
Write immutable artifacts with exclusive creation, fsync each file, verify bytes against the manifest, then fsync the staging directory.
Write final receipt last with state FINALIZING; fsync it and atomically rename the complete staging directory to a content-addressed committed directory on the same filesystem.
Append the receipt index only after the directory rename using compare-and-swap on the previous index digest, then fsync the index directory.
A reader accepts only a committed directory whose final receipt, manifest, and index binding all verify. Partial staging directories are never evidence.
receipt_bundle.retention: Committed redacted bundles are append-only and retained according to the sealed retention policy. Deletion, legal hold, or cryptographic-erasure requests create a signed tombstone that retains identity, digests, authority, and reason without rewriting prior receipts.

state_machine: PREPARED -> DISCOVERING -> DISCOVERY_SEALED -> EXECUTING -> PARSING -> RECONCILING -> COMMITTED
Any state -> BLOCKED when authority, integrity, environment, privacy, parser, source-binding, or budget invariants fail.
BLOCKED -> DIAGNOSE -> REMEDIATE -> REVALIDATE only under a recovery lease, bounded recovery contract, and preserved predecessor evidence.
REVALIDATE -> COMMITTED | BLOCKED; it creates a new attempt/session and never edits the blocked receipt.
BLOCKED -> ESCALATED when bounded retries, remediation authority, budget, or safety conditions are exhausted.
recovery_protocol.diagnose: Records a machine-classified blocker, exact checkpoint, source/runtime bindings, and evidence references. It may inspect declared artifacts but may not infer missing outcomes or broaden authority.
recovery_protocol.remediate: Consumes only a separately authorized reversible remediation action. It must declare scope, rollback, idempotency key, expected evidence, and candidate applicability before execution. A recorder incident does not grant code, plan, candidate, CI, promotion, or remote authority.
recovery_protocol.revalidate: Replays discovery and validation in a new sealed session against a newly bound target. It retains both attempts, performs no statistical/performance conclusion, and emits a linkage record rather than a replacement.

bounded_retry_and_escalation.blocker_signature: sha256 of normalized failure class, invariant, source binding, runner contract digest, and declared environment class
bounded_retry_and_escalation.escalation: On repeated signature, missing authority, destructive/sensitive remediation, or exhausted budget, emit an ESCALATED receipt with all prior links and open an evidence-backed decision record. Escalation is not a human-approval substitute and does not permit recursive unbounded courts.

record: candidate_id, candidate_commit, candidate_tree, parent_commit, component_kind, changed_path_manifest_digest, source_target_commit, source_target_tree, required_composition, governing_case, authority_status, rejection_or_promotion_status, required_validation_contract_digest, comparator_receipts, rollback_reference
invariants: A candidate is applicable only when its exact commit/tree, declared component kind, validation target commit/tree, required composition, authority status, and validation contract all match the sealed applicability predicate.
Candidate lineage, a similarly named API, or a passing focused test never implies applicability.
Rejected, quarantined, non-promoted, or explicitly ineligible candidates fail applicability before execution and are retained as negative evidence.
Composition is an explicit new candidate record with its own commit/tree, authority, rollback, and independent validation; a recorder never combines historical candidates implicitly.
candidate_applicability.historical_guard: 41950b74bdec2b6e1c48ee7f5ef3ce947d0c8378 and d02c2d2 remain adverse/ineligible as specified by their courts. This design neither changes their status nor permits reuse, relabeling, qualification, or composition.

inputs: Sealed ValidationRunContract from the control plane
Versioned discovery adapter and event-emitting runner adapter
outputs: Immutable content-addressed discovery vector, terminal ledger, parser, reconciliation, and redacted stream artifacts
Blocked, invalid, or escalated evidence reference when final validation cannot be proven
explicit_non_capabilities: No direct shell, repository, network, secret, Git ref, plan, candidate, or promotion authority.
No interpretation of text output outside the sealed event grammar.
No overwriting, deletion, or mutation of a prior receipt.
No verdict, merge, self-approval, or conversion of a validation result into implementation authority.
api_boundary.versioning: Adapters negotiate major schema version only. Unknown major versions, optional fields that affect accounting, or lossy down-conversion fail closed.

migration: Introduce the native recorder behind a new adapter capability; retain existing portable receipt validation unchanged.
Run in shadow-capture mode only under a separately authorized implementation/evaluation plan; shadow receipts never replace existing evidence.
Promote an adapter only after independent tests demonstrate all invariants and a separate court approves the implementation.
migration_and_rollback.legacy_behavior: Legacy transcript receipts remain readable as historical artifacts, but absence of a native discovery vector, terminal ledger, vocabulary, or reconciliation is represented as unknown, not backfilled.
migration_and_rollback.rollback: Disable the new adapter capability and revert only its implementation commit under a separately authorized rollback. Preserve every native receipt, blocked session, redaction record, rejection, and migration mapping append-only.

unit_contract_tests: Reject duplicate/unknown discovery IDs and nonportable artifact paths.
Reject missing, duplicate, contradictory, or out-of-order terminal outcomes.
Expand class and lifecycle skips to one ledger record per discovered affected ID.
Reject undeclared labels, grammar mutation, malformed JSONL, stream digest mismatch, and post-hoc vocabulary changes.
Prove all summary equations and that NOT_RUN states cannot be counted as passes or executed tests.
Exercise redaction without leaking candidate secrets into retained artifacts, exceptions, metrics, or hashes visible to the repository.
durability_and_recovery_tests: Inject crash cuts before/after every fsync, rename, and index compare-and-swap; readers must see either no receipt or one valid committed receipt.
Prove duplicate idempotency keys do not create duplicate terminal ledgers.
Prove BLOCKED -> DIAGNOSE -> REMEDIATE -> REVALIDATE preserves all predecessor evidence and respects retry bounds.
Prove blocked candidates cannot become applicable by naming or composition alone.
integration_tests: Use a synthetic event-emitting runner with pass, failure, explicit skip, class skip, lifecycle skip, abort, output diagnostics, and malformed-stream cases.
Verify repository/worktree, interpreter, environment, and authority bindings change when inputs change.
Independently reproduce a committed receipt from immutable artifacts in a clean workspace without raw secret access.

acceptance_metrics.summary_reconciliation_rate: 100% for completed runner summaries; mismatch count must be zero for VALIDATED_* receipts
acceptance_metrics.privacy_leak_rate: 0 confirmed secret values in repository-retained artifacts
acceptance_metrics.atomicity_violation_rate: 0 accepted partial/duplicate bundles under injected crash tests
acceptance_metrics.unbounded_recovery_rate: 0; every recurrence must escalate at configured bounds

material_design_risks.risk: Runner frameworks may not expose class/lifecycle skips per method.
material_design_risks.control: The native adapter must emit structured affected-ID events from the sealed vector; unsupported runners are BLOCKED, not text-parsed heuristically.

material_design_risks.risk: Raw output can contain secrets or personal/proprietary data.
material_design_risks.control: Protected capture and pre-retention redaction separate raw stream integrity from repository artifacts; a redaction failure blocks finalization.

material_design_risks.risk: A technically complete receipt could be mistaken for a passing delivery or court judgment.
material_design_risks.control: Receipt result, authority reference, candidate applicability, and court dispositions are separate typed fields; the API has no promotion or judgment operation.

material_design_risks.risk: Automatic recovery may recreate the recursive-governance loop.
material_design_risks.control: Recovery is a bounded state machine with blocker signatures, finite budgets, and an escalated decision record rather than automatic successor courts.

implementation_boundary.authorized_by_this_record: Architecture and later independent review only.
not_authorized_by_this_record: Tests, fixtures, controller changes, CI, discovery, candidate execution, or performance measurements
Reuse, relabeling, qualification, or composition of 41950b74bdec2b6e1c48ee7f5ef3ce947d0c8378 or d02c2d2
implementation_boundary.next_authority_requirement: Only a separate newly sealed native implementation-proposal DAG, after independent cross-examination and a Judge finds zero unresolved material design findings, may propose bounded implementation work.
